correctness.rationale: In the E_xy basis, site-projector dephasing is a diagonal waiting weight, so a trace term of flux harmonic ℓ needs at least N|ℓ| actual hops. The transpose-and-coordinate-swap identity maps the commutator to its negative without changing the symmetric diagonal dissipator. On odd rings, −H is gauge equivalent to H at flux shifted by π; hence both full and coherent moments have only even harmonics. At the respective first allowed orders N and 2N, nonconstant harmonics cannot use any waits. For the coherent trace, the left/right binomial expansion yields two endpoint terms at even order N. At odd order 2N, only indices 0, N, 2N can contribute: a one-winding Hamiltonian trace at odd order greater than N multiplies a zero odd trace below N. The h_N squared term and two h_(2N) terms produce precisely the binomial-minus-two factor with a negative sign. This verifies the unnormalized trace, the flux zeros, and independence from arbitrary fixed nonuniform or zero dephasing rates. The odd π shift relates isospectral generators through sign reversal plus gauge, not by identifying H_π with H_0 alone.
residual_risks: The exact proof uses pure site-projector dephasing and no diagonal Hamiltonian energies; the numerical corroboration is finite.

value.rationale: The full trace moments give a basis-independent test of when a spectrum can begin to see magnetic holonomy. Odd parity doubles the minimum order notwithstanding single-coordinate windings at order N, and attaining the sharp order rules out all influence from arbitrary sitewise dephasing on the exact first response. This is a structural parity threshold and closed quantitative invariant, not a calculation for a hand-selected rate profile.
residual_risks: Spectral statement only, not a bound on relaxation or a flux measurement protocol.
